question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Words inscribed on a tombstone in memory of a dead person.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Epitaph.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Epitaph" means words written on a grave, from Greek epitaphios, from epi- (upon) and taphos (tomb). (समाधिलेख)
◦ Example: The epitaph on the ancient tomb was barely legible after centuries of weathering.

 

• Do not confuse Epitaph (inscription on a grave) with Epigraph (an inscription on a building or a quotation at the start of a book or chapter).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Elegy (शोक गीत): A mournful poem or song, especially one written for the dead.

 

• Option 3: Eulogy (प्रशंसा भाषण): A speech or piece of writing praising someone highly, typically one who has died.

 

• Option 4: Obituary (मृत्युलेख): A published notice of a person's death, often with a short biography.

 

NOTE

 

• Related death/memorial words: Elegy (a mournful poem for the dead), Eulogy (a speech praising the dead), Obituary (a published notice of death), Requiem (a mass or music for the dead), Cenotaph (a monument to someone buried elsewhere).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others to gain advantage

2. Ostentatious (दिखावटी): Characterized by pretentious display

3. Nostalgia (भूतकाल की याद): A sentimental longing for the past

4. Philanthropist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person who works for the welfare of others, especially through charity

5. Xenophobia (विदेशी-भय): Intense dislike or fear of foreigners

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Describing a fault or offense that is minor and easily excused.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Venial.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Venial" means a minor, excusable fault, from Latin venia, meaning pardon or forgiveness. (क्षम्य)
◦ Example: Forgetting to reply to an email is a venial lapse, not a serious offense.

 

• In religious and moral usage, Venial sin (pardonable) is contrasted with Mortal sin (grave and unpardonable without repentance) — remember this pair for SSC vocabulary questions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Heinous (जघन्य): Utterly wicked or shockingly evil, used for terrible crimes.

 

• Option 2: Mortal (घातक): Causing death, or, of a sin, considered gravely serious and unpardonable.

 

• Option 3: Cardinal (प्रधान): Of the greatest importance; fundamental.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast with: Mortal (extremely serious, deadly), Heinous (shockingly wicked), Cardinal (chief or most important) — these are commonly used as antonym-type distractors for Venial.

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Altruism (परार्थवाद): Selfless concern for the well-being of others

2. Benevolent (दयालु): Well-meaning and kindly

3. Candid (स्पष्टवादी): Truthful and straightforward

4. Deft (निपुण): Neatly skillful and quick in action

5. Ephemeral (क्षणभंगुर): Lasting for a very short time

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The practice of a woman being married to more than one husband at the same time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Polyandry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Polyandry" means a woman having multiple husbands, from Greek poly (many) and andros (man, husband). (बहुपति प्रथा)
◦ Example: Polyandry is practiced in certain communities in the Himalayan regions.

 

• Remember: -andry relates to a man or husband, so Polyandry means many husbands, while -gyny relates to a woman or wife, so Polygyny means many wives.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Polygamy (बहुविवाह प्रथा): The practice of having more than one spouse at the same time, a general term.

 

• Option 3: Polygyny (बहुपत्नी प्रथा): The practice of a man having more than one wife.

 

• Option 4: Monogamy (एकविवाह प्रथा): The practice of being married to only one person at a time.

 

NOTE

 

• Marriage-related family words: Polygamy (multiple spouses in general), Polygyny (many wives), Monogamy (one spouse), Bigamy (marrying two people at once, often illegal), Endogamy (marrying within one's own group), Exogamy (marrying outside one's group).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Frugal (मितव्ययी): Sparing or economical with money and resources

2. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Fond of company; sociable

3. Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is the most important goal in life

4. Impeccable (निर्दोष): Flawless; without any mistake

5. Jubilant (हर्षित): Feeling or expressing great happiness

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Possessing unlimited or complete power over all things.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Omnipotent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Omnipotent" means having unlimited power, from Latin omni- (all) and potens (powerful). (सर्वशक्तिमान)
◦ Example: In many religions, God is described as omnipotent, omniscient, and omnipresent.

 

• The prefix "omni-" means "all"; learn the trio together — Omnipotent (all-powerful), Omniscient (all-knowing), Omnipresent (present everywhere).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Omniscient (सर्वज्ञ): Knowing everything.

 

• Option 3: Omnipresent (सर्वव्यापी): Present everywhere at the same time.

 

• Option 4: Omnivorous (सर्वभक्षी): Eating both plant and animal food.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "omni-" words: Omniscient (all-knowing), Omnipresent (everywhere at once), Omnivorous (eating everything, plant and animal), Omnibus (covering many items at once, e.g. an omnibus bill).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Knack (हुनर): A special skill or ability to do something easily

2. Latent (सुप्त): Existing but not yet developed or manifest

3. Malinger (बीमारी का बहाना करना): To pretend to be ill in order to avoid work

4. Nonchalant (उदासीन): Calm and casual, showing no anxiety

5. Obdurate (हठी): Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Willing to comply with or respond positively to guidance or authority.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Amenable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Amenable" means willing to agree or obey, from French amener (to lead), ultimately from Latin minare (to drive). (आज्ञाकारी)
◦ Example: The new employee was amenable to feedback and quickly improved his work.

 

• Amenable is often followed by "to" (amenable to suggestion or reason); its opposites are Recalcitrant and Obstinate.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Obstinate (हठी): Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action.

 

• Option 3: Truculent (उग्र): Eager or quick to argue or fight; aggressively defiant.

 

• Option 4: Recalcitrant (अवज्ञाकारी): Having an obstinately uncooperative attitude toward authority.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast with words for stubbornness: Obstinate (unyielding), Recalcitrant (defiant of authority), Truculent (aggressively defiant), Intransigent (refusing to compromise).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Placate (शांत करना): To calm someone's anger or make them less hostile

2. Quandary (दुविधा): A state of perplexity or difficult choice

3. Sagacious (बुद्धिमान): Wise, showing good judgment

4. Reticent (मितभाषी): Reserved, not revealing thoughts or feelings readily

5. Truculent (झगड़ालू): Aggressively defiant and eager to argue

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Believing that all people should have equal rights and opportunities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Egalitarian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Egalitarian" means believing all people are equal, from French egal (equal). (समतावादी)
◦ Example: She held egalitarian views and campaigned for equal pay for equal work.

 

• Egalitarian is the opposite of Elitist; remembering the root "equal" helps recall the meaning quickly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Elitist (अभिजात्यवादी): A person who believes a select group of superior people should have power or influence.

 

• Option 3: Autocrat (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler who has absolute power, unrestrained by others.

 

• Option 4: Plutocrat (धनी शासक): A person who is powerful because of their wealth.

 

NOTE

 

• Political/social belief words: Elitist (favoring a superior few), Autocrat (one-person absolute rule), Plutocrat (rule by the wealthy), Meritocrat (rule by talent or achievement), Anarchist (believer in no government).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ubiquitous (सर्वव्यापी): Present, appearing, or found everywhere

2. Verbose (शब्दाडंबरपूर्ण): Using more words than needed

3. Whimsical (तरंगी): Playfully quaint or fanciful in manner

4. Yearn (तड़पना): To have an intense feeling of longing for something

5. Zealot (कट्टरपंथी): A fanatical and uncompromising follower of a cause

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes in and worships more than one god.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Polytheist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Polytheist" means believer in many gods, from Greek poly (many) and theos (god). (अनेक देवताओं में विश्वास करने वाला)
◦ Example: Ancient Greek and Roman societies were largely polytheist, worshipping many gods.

 

• Group belief-related words by the root "theos" (god): Monotheist (one god), Polytheist (many gods), Atheist (no god), Agnostic (unknowable).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Atheist (नास्तिक): A person who does not believe in the existence of God or gods.

 

• Option 2: Monotheist (एकेश्वरवादी): A person who believes in only one God.

 

• Option 3: Agnostic (अज्ञेयवादी): A person who believes it is not possible to know whether God exists.

 

NOTE

 

• Belief-system words: Atheist (disbelieves in God), Monotheist (believes in one God), Agnostic (believes God's existence is unknowable), Pantheist (believes God and universe are one), Theist (believes in the existence of God generally).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Abstemious (संयमी): Sparing or moderate in eating and drinking

2. Belligerent (आक्रामक): Hostile and aggressive

3. Congenial (अनुकूल): Pleasant or agreeable, especially in atmosphere or company

4. Debacle (करारी हार): A sudden and ignominious failure

5. Effervescent (जोशीला): Vivacious and full of enthusiasm

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An irresistible urge to steal, not motivated by need.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Kleptomania.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Kleptomania" means uncontrollable urge to steal, from Greek klepto- (to steal) and mania (madness). (चोरी की बीमारी)
◦ Example: The wealthy woman was diagnosed with kleptomania after repeatedly shoplifting items she didn't need.

 

• The suffix "-mania" denotes an excessive or uncontrollable urge or obsession — identify the root before it to know what the urge is about.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Pyromania (अग्नि लगाने का उन्माद): An uncontrollable urge to start fires.

 

• Option 3: Megalomania (महत्वोन्माद): An obsession with one's own power, importance, or grandeur.

 

• Option 4: Dipsomania (मद्यपान की उत्कट लालसा): An uncontrollable craving for alcoholic drink.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-mania" words: Pyromania (urge to set fires), Megalomania (obsession with grandeur or power), Dipsomania (craving for alcohol), Monomania (obsession with one single thing).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Fastidious (नकचढ़ा): Very attentive to detail and hard to please

2. Garrulous (बातूनी): Excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters

3. Harbinger (अग्रदूत): A person or thing that signals the approach of something

4. Iconoclast (परंपरा भंजक): One who attacks cherished beliefs or traditional institutions

5. Jovial (प्रफुल्लित): Cheerful and friendly in mood

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An attitude of excessive pride or self-importance, often with contempt for others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Arrogance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Arrogance" means excessive pride and self-importance, from Latin arrogare (to claim for oneself). (घमंड)
◦ Example: His arrogance made it hard for colleagues to work with him.

 

• Arrogance is the direct opposite of Humility and Modesty — a favorite antonym pair in SSC vocabulary questions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Humility (विनम्रता): A modest or low view of one's own importance.

 

• Option 2: Diffidence (आत्म-अविश्वास): Lack of self-confidence; shyness in putting oneself forward.

 

• Option 4: Modesty (शालीनता): The quality of not being too proud or boastful about oneself.

 

NOTE

 

• Contrast set: Humility (modesty), Diffidence (shyness or lack of confidence), Modesty (unassuming nature), Vanity (excessive pride in appearance), Hubris (excessive pride or self-confidence, especially leading to downfall).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Lament (विलाप करना): To express passionate grief or sorrow

2. Myopic (अदूरदर्शी): Lacking foresight or imagination; short-sighted

3. Nadir (निम्नतम बिंदु): The lowest or most unsuccessful point of a situation

4. Obsequious (खुशामदी): Excessively eager to please or obey

5. Knell (मृत्यु घंटी): The sound of a bell rung solemnly, especially for a death

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A reduction in the severity or duration of a punishment or a disease.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Remission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Remission" means reduction of punishment or illness, from Latin remittere (to send back, relax). (दंड मुक्ति)
◦ Example: The prisoner received a remission of his sentence for good behavior.

 

• Remission is used both in legal contexts (a reduced sentence) and medical contexts (disease symptoms lessening) — note this dual usage for SSC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reprieve (सज़ा का अस्थायी स्थगन): A temporary postponement of a punishment, especially execution.

 

• Option 2: Amnesty (आम क्षमा): An official pardon for people convicted of political offenses, granted generally.

 

• Option 4: Acquittal (दोषमुक्ति): A judicial verdict that a person is not guilty of the charge.

 

NOTE

 

• Legal pardon-related words: Reprieve (temporary postponement of punishment), Amnesty (general pardon), Acquittal (found not guilty), Parole (early conditional release from prison), Clemency (mercy shown by an authority).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Panacea (सर्वरोगहर औषधि): A solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases

2. Quagmire (कठिन परिस्थिति): A difficult, complex, or precarious situation

3. Rancor (द्वेष): Bitterness or resentfulness, especially long-lasting

4. Sanguine (आशावादी): Optimistic or positive, especially in a difficult situation

5. Taciturn (अल्पभाषी): Reserved or uncommunicative in speech

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Speaking fluently, readily, and at great length.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Voluble.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Voluble" means talking a lot, fluently, from Latin volvere (to roll), suggesting words rolling easily off the tongue. (बहुत बोलने वाला)
◦ Example: The voluble guide talked continuously throughout the entire tour.

 

• Voluble is the opposite of Taciturn, Reticent, and Laconic — all of which mean speaking little; this antonym cluster is a common SSC trap.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reticent (संकोची): Not revealing one's thoughts or feelings readily; reserved.

 

• Option 2: Taciturn (अल्पभाषी): Reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little.

 

• Option 4: Laconic (संक्षिप्तवादी): Using very few words to express something.

 

NOTE

 

• Speech-related antonyms: Taciturn (saying little), Reticent (reserved about sharing), Laconic (using few words), Garrulous (excessively talkative, like Voluble), Loquacious (very talkative).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Umbrage (नाराज़गी): A feeling of offense or annoyance

2. Vindicate (निर्दोष सिद्ध करना): To clear someone of blame or suspicion

3. Wanderlust (घुमक्कड़ी की चाह): A strong desire to travel and explore the world

4. Xenophile (विदेशी-प्रेमी): A person attracted to foreign peoples, cultures, or customs

5. Docile (आज्ञाकारी): Ready to accept control or instruction; easily managed

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A formal expression of warm and high praise.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Encomium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Encomium" means expression of high praise, from Greek enkomion, praise of a person, originally at a victory celebration. (प्रशंसा)
◦ Example: The chairman delivered an encomium on the retiring professor's decades of service.

 

• Encomium (praise) is the opposite of Diatribe and Tirade (harsh criticism) — a common antonym-based SSC option set.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Diatribe (निंदा भाषण): A forceful and bitter verbal attack against someone or something.

 

• Option 2: Tirade (क्रोधपूर्ण भाषण): A long, angry speech of criticism or accusation.

 

• Option 4: Eulogy (श्रद्धांजलि भाषण): A speech or piece of writing praising someone highly, typically one who has died.

 

NOTE

 

• Praise-and-criticism words: Eulogy (praise, often for the dead), Panegyric (formal public praise), Diatribe (bitter attack), Tirade (angry critical speech), Invective (abusive or insulting language).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Zenith (चरम बिंदु): The highest point or peak of something

2. Abhor (घृणा करना): To regard with disgust and hatred

3. Bereft (वंचित): Deprived of or lacking something

4. Cajole (फुसलाना): To persuade someone through flattery or coaxing

5. Impetuous (उतावला): Acting quickly without thought or care

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A specialist in the study, identification, and grading of precious stones.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Gemologist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Gemologist" means expert in the study of gemstones, from Latin gemma (gem) and Greek logos (study). (रत्न विशेषज्ञ)
◦ Example: The gemologist examined the diamond carefully under a jeweler's loupe.

 

• Do not confuse Gemologist (studies gemstones) with the similar-sounding Geologist (studies rocks and the earth's structure).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Geologist (भूवैज्ञानिक): A person who studies the physical structure and substance of the earth.

 

• Option 2: Numismatist (मुद्राशास्त्री): A person who studies or collects coins and currency.

 

• Option 3: Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects and studies postage stamps.

 

NOTE

 

• Study/collector words with suffix -ist/-ologist: Numismatist (coins), Philatelist (stamps), Geologist (earth and rocks), Archivist (records and documents), Ornithologist (birds).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ebullient (उत्साहपूर्ण): Cheerful and full of energy

2. Facetious (मज़ाकिया): Treating serious things with inappropriate humor

3. Gullible (भोला): Easily deceived or tricked

4. Hackneyed (घिसा-पिटा): Overused and unoriginal

5. Jargon (विशेष शब्दावली): Special terminology used within a particular profession or group

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A feeling of deep and profound respect for someone or something.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Reverence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Reverence" means deep respect and admiration, from Latin revereri (to stand in awe of). (आदर)
◦ Example: The students treated their teacher with great reverence.

 

• Reverence is the opposite of Contempt, Disdain, and Derision — all of which express disrespect or scorn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Contempt (तिरस्कार): A feeling that a person or thing deserves scorn or is beneath consideration.

 

• Option 3: Disdain (उपेक्षा): The feeling that someone or something is unworthy of one's consideration.

 

• Option 4: Derision (उपहास): Contemptuous ridicule or mockery.

 

NOTE

 

• Respect vs disrespect words: Contempt (scorn), Disdain (feeling of unworthiness), Derision (mockery), Veneration (deep respect, similar to reverence), Awe (respectful wonder).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Kudos (श्रेय): Praise and honor received for an achievement

2. Lucrative (लाभदायक): Producing a great deal of profit

3. Meager (अल्प): Lacking in quantity or quality

4. Nostrum (झूठा उपाय): An ineffective medicine or remedy sold as a solution

5. Pariah (बहिष्कृत व्यक्ति): An outcast, a person despised or rejected by others

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Extremely generous, especially in giving money or gifts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Munificent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Munificent" means extremely generous in giving, from Latin munificus (bountiful), from munus (gift) and facere (to make). (उदार)
◦ Example: The munificent donor funded the entire new library wing.

 

• Munificent is the opposite of Parsimonious and Miserly — remember it alongside its near-synonym Generous.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Parsimonious (अत्यधिक मितव्ययी): Extremely unwilling to spend money or use resources.

 

• Option 3: Miserly (कृपण): Extremely stingy with money.

 

• Option 4: Frugal (किफायती): Sparing or economical with money or resources.

 

NOTE

 

• Spending-related words: Parsimonious (stingy), Miserly (extremely stingy), Frugal (economical, not wasteful), Prodigal (wastefully extravagant), Lavish (giving generously and abundantly).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Oblivious (बेखबर): Not aware of or not attentive to what is happening

2. Quibble (छोटी-छोटी बातों पर बहस करना): To argue or complain about trivial matters

3. Rebuff (इनकार): A blunt or curt refusal or rejection

4. Stoic (धैर्यवान): One who endures hardship or pain without complaint

5. Culpable (दोषी): Deserving blame for a wrongdoing

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Persistently diligent and hardworking, showing great care and attention.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Assiduous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Assiduous" means hardworking and diligent, from Latin assiduus (constantly present), from assidere (to sit down to). (परिश्रमी)
◦ Example: Her assiduous preparation helped her top the competitive exam.

 

• Assiduous is the opposite of Indolent, Lethargic, and Languid — all suggesting laziness or lack of energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Indolent (आलसी): Wanting to avoid activity or exertion; lazy.

 

• Option 3: Lethargic (सुस्त): Sluggish and lacking energy.

 

• Option 4: Languid (शिथिल): Displaying a lack of vigor or disinclination for effort.

 

NOTE

 

• Diligence vs laziness words: Indolent (lazy), Lethargic (sluggish), Languid (lacking vigor), Diligent (careful and persistent, similar to Assiduous), Industrious (hardworking).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Tenacious (दृढ़): Holding firmly to a course of action or belief

2. Usurp (हड़पना): To seize power or a position wrongfully

3. Vex (परेशान करना): To annoy or irritate someone

4. Wary (सतर्क): Cautious of danger or possible trouble

5. Yoke (बंधन): A bond or restraint linking two things together

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

So extraordinary or implausible as to be difficult to believe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Incredible.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Incredible" means too extraordinary to believe, from Latin in- (not) and credibilis (believable, from credere, to believe). (अविश्वसनीय)
◦ Example: It seemed incredible that anyone could survive such a fall unharmed.

 

• The prefix "in-" negates the base word, so Incredible (not believable) is the direct opposite of Credible (believable).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Credible (विश्वसनीय): Able to be believed; convincing.

 

• Option 2: Plausible (संभाव्य): Seeming reasonable or probable.

 

• Option 3: Veracious (सत्यनिष्ठ): Habitually speaking the truth; truthful.

 

NOTE

 

• Root "cred-" (belief) family: Credible (believable), Credulous (too ready to believe), Incredulous (unwilling to believe), Discredit (to harm reputation or cause disbelief), Creed (a set of beliefs).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Zealous (उत्साही): Showing great enthusiasm and eagerness

2. Abate (कम होना): To become less intense or widespread

3. Brevity (संक्षिप्तता): Concise and exact use of words

4. Cacophony (कर्कश ध्वनि): A harsh, discordant mixture of sounds

5. Deride (उपहास करना): To express contempt for someone through mockery

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A form of government in which power is held by a small, privileged, upper-class group.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Aristocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aristocracy" means rule by the privileged upper class, from Greek aristos (best) and kratos (power, rule). (कुलीनतंत्र)
◦ Example: Before the revolution, France was ruled by an aristocracy of nobles and landowners.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" means "rule or government by" — identify the root before it to know who rules.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Democracy (लोकतंत्र): A system of government by the whole population, typically through elected representatives.

 

• Option 2: Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): A system of government by religious leaders, claiming divine guidance.

 

• Option 3: Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): A system of government administered by officials and departments.

 

NOTE

 

• "-cracy" family: Democracy (rule by the people), Theocracy (rule by religion), Bureaucracy (rule by officials), Plutocracy (rule by the wealthy), Autocracy (rule by one person with absolute power), Meritocracy (rule by the talented).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Erudite (विद्वान): Having or showing great knowledge or learning

2. Facade (बाहरी दिखावा): A false outward appearance concealing something less pleasant

3. Gaunt (दुबला-पतला): Thin and haggard, especially from suffering or hunger

4. Homage (श्रद्धांजलि): Special honor or respect shown publicly

5. Impervious (असंवेदनशील): Not affected or influenced by something

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A state of being stunned, confused, or unable to think clearly, often after a shock.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Daze.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Daze" means a confused, stunned state. (स्तब्ध अवस्था)
◦ Example: After the accident, she wandered around in a daze, unable to speak.

 

• Daze is usually used in the phrase "in a daze" and can also function as a verb meaning to stun someone into confusion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Delirium (प्रलाप): A disturbed state of mind, often with incoherent speech, restlessness, and hallucinations.

 

• Option 2: Stupor (मूर्च्छा): A state of near-unconsciousness or greatly dulled senses.

 

• Option 4: Trance (तंद्रा): A half-conscious state in which one is not fully aware of one's surroundings.

 

NOTE

 

• Confused/unconscious states: Stupor (near-unconsciousness), Delirium (incoherent disturbed state), Trance (dreamlike half-conscious state), Bewilderment (confusion), Stupefaction (state of being stunned).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Jubilee (उत्सव): A special anniversary celebration, especially of a significant event

2. Knave (बदमाश): A dishonest or unscrupulous man

3. Lethargy (सुस्ती): A lack of energy and enthusiasm

4. Malaise (अस्वस्थता): A general feeling of discomfort or unease

5. Nemesis (चिर शत्रु): A long-standing rival, or an agent of someone's downfall

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

To destroy or remove something completely, root and all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Extirpate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Extirpate" means to destroy completely, from Latin exstirpare, from ex- (out) and stirps (root, stem), literally to root out. (नष्ट करना)
◦ Example: The government launched a campaign to extirpate corruption from public offices.

 

• Extirpate literally means "to root out" — think of pulling a plant out by its roots to remember its meaning of complete destruction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Instigate (उकसाना): To bring about an action, especially something bad, by inciting others.

 

• Option 2: Perpetuate (चिरस्थायी बनाना): To make something continue indefinitely; to preserve from extinction.

 

• Option 4: Propagate (प्रचार करना): To spread and promote an idea widely, or to breed and multiply.

 

NOTE

 

• Words for destruction and removal: Eradicate (to eliminate completely, especially disease), Annihilate (to destroy utterly), Obliterate (to remove all trace of), Eliminate (to remove or get rid of), Exterminate (to destroy completely, especially a group).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Onus (उत्तरदायित्व): A duty or responsibility that falls on someone

2. Placid (शांत): Calm and peaceful, not easily disturbed

3. Querulous (शिकायती): Complaining in a petulant or whining manner

4. Rapport (मधुर संबंध): A close and harmonious relationship

5. Somber (गंभीर): Dark, gloomy, and serious in mood

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Open to more than one interpretation; not having one clear meaning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ambiguous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ambiguous" means having more than one possible meaning, from Latin ambigere (to wander, go about), from ambi- (both ways) and agere (to drive). (अस्पष्ट)
◦ Example: His ambiguous answer left the committee unsure of his true intentions.

 

• Ambiguous is the opposite of Unequivocal, Explicit, and Lucid — all of which mean clearly and singularly understood.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Unequivocal (असंदिग्ध): Leaving no doubt; having only one possible interpretation.

 

• Option 3: Explicit (स्पष्ट): Stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing implied.

 

• Option 4: Lucid (सुबोध): Expressed clearly; easy to understand.

 

NOTE

 

• Clarity-related antonyms: Unequivocal (leaving no doubt), Explicit (clearly stated), Lucid (easy to understand), Vague (unclear and imprecise, similar to Ambiguous), Equivocal (open to more than one interpretation, near-synonym).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Turbulent (अशांत): Marked by conflict, disorder, or confusion

2. Unkempt (अस्त-व्यस्त): Untidy, not neatly maintained

3. Venerate (श्रद्धा करना): To regard with great respect and reverence

4. Wistful (उदासीन लालसा से भरा): Having a feeling of vague or regretful longing

5. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to and inexperienced in a field

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The scientific study of human beings, their societies, and cultures, past and present.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Anthropology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anthropology" means study of humans and their cultures, from Greek anthropos (human being) and logos (study). (मानवशास्त्र)
◦ Example: She pursued a degree in anthropology to understand tribal customs across the world.

 

• The root "anthropo-" means "human" — found also in words like Anthropomorphic (giving human qualities to non-human things) and Misanthrope (one who hates humankind).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Archaeology (पुरातत्वशास्त्र): The study of human history through the excavation and analysis of artifacts and physical remains.

 

• Option 3: Ethnology (नृजातिविज्ञान): The branch of study that compares and analyzes the characteristics of different peoples.

 

• Option 4: Sociology (समाजशास्त्र): The study of the development, structure, and functioning of human society.

 

NOTE

 

• Social science study words: Archaeology (past human artifacts), Sociology (society), Ethnology (comparative study of peoples), Ethnography (descriptive study of a specific culture), Demography (study of population statistics).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Boisterous (उग्र): Noisy, energetic, and lacking restraint

2. Emaciated (अत्यंत दुर्बल): Abnormally thin, especially from illness or hunger

3. Fecund (उर्वर): Fertile and productive, capable of generating abundant growth

4. Heredity (आनुवंशिकता): The passing of physical or mental traits from parents to offspring

5. Innate (जन्मजात): Inborn and natural rather than acquired

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A genetic condition in which one chromosome of a pair is missing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Monosomy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Monosomy" means missing one chromosome of a pair, from Greek mono- (single) and soma (body, referring to the chromosome). (गुणसूत्र कमी)
◦ Example: Turner syndrome is an example of monosomy, where a female has only one X chromosome.

 

• Monosomy (one chromosome missing) is the opposite of Trisomy (one extra chromosome) — both fall under the broader term Aneuploidy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Trisomy (त्रिगुणसूत्रता): A chromosomal condition in which there is an extra copy of a chromosome, three instead of two.

 

• Option 2: Aneuploidy (असामान्य गुणसूत्र संख्या): A general condition of having an abnormal number of chromosomes, extra or missing.

 

• Option 3: Polyploidy (बहुगुणिता): A condition in which an organism has more than two complete sets of chromosomes.

 

NOTE

 

• Chromosomal condition words: Trisomy (extra chromosome, e.g. Down syndrome), Aneuploidy (abnormal chromosome number generally), Polyploidy (extra full sets of chromosomes), Euploidy (normal chromosome number).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Gestation (गर्भावस्था): The process of developing inside the womb before birth

2. Abrogate (रद्द करना): To repeal or do away with a law or agreement formally

3. Diligent (मेहनती): Showing careful and persistent effort in one's work

4. Pensive (चिंतनशील): Engaged in deep or serious thought

5. Opulent (वैभवशाली): Luxurious and lavish in style or possessions

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Lacking any organization or order; done randomly, without planning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Haphazard.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Haphazard" means done randomly, without planning, from Arabic az-zahr via Old French hasard (chance, dice), meaning left to chance. (अव्यवस्थित)
◦ Example: The files were stored in a haphazard manner, making it hard to find anything.

 

• Haphazard is the opposite of Methodical, Systematic, and Meticulous — all of which indicate careful organization.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Methodical (व्यवस्थित): Done according to a systematic or organized method.

 

• Option 2: Systematic (क्रमबद्ध): Done according to a fixed plan or system, in a methodical way.

 

• Option 4: Meticulous (सूक्ष्मता से किया गया): Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.

 

NOTE

 

• Order vs disorder words: Methodical (organized method), Systematic (planned system), Meticulous (careful attention to detail), Random (without a definite pattern, similar to Haphazard), Chaotic (in complete disorder).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Jettison (त्यागना): To throw away or discard something no longer needed

2. Knotty (जटिल): Difficult or complicated to deal with

3. Lull (शांति का दौर): A temporary period of quiet or calm during a stormy or busy time

4. Meander (घुमावदार रास्ते से जाना): To wander aimlessly without a fixed direction

5. Quaint (विचित्र किंतु आकर्षक): Attractively unusual or old-fashioned

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Tending to induce sleep or drowsiness.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Soporific.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Soporific" means causing sleep or drowsiness, from Latin sopor (deep sleep) and -ficus (making). (निद्राजनक)
◦ Example: The professor's monotonous lecture had a soporific effect on the students.

 

• The root "sopor-" relates to sleep; note the contrast with Insomniac (cannot sleep) and Somnambulist (walks while asleep).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Insomniac (अनिद्रा रोगी): A person who habitually finds it difficult to sleep.

 

• Option 3: Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला): A person who walks around while asleep; a sleepwalker.

 

• Option 4: Vigilant (सतर्क): Keeping careful watch for possible danger; alert.

 

NOTE

 

• Sleep-related words: Insomniac (cannot sleep), Somnambulist (sleepwalker), Narcoleptic (suffers from sudden urges to sleep), Lethargic (lacking energy, sluggish), Hypnotic (inducing sleep, similar to Soporific).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ravenous (अत्यंत भूखा): Extremely hungry

2. Sullen (उदास): Bad-tempered and gloomily silent

3. Impervious (अभेद्य): Not able to be affected or penetrated

4. Candid (स्पष्टवादी): Truthful and straightforward in speech

5. Zestful (उत्साहपूर्ण): Full of energy and enthusiasm
